title: Credit Manager - Recruitment Business
company: Bond Moran Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Senior Credit Control Manager - Recruitment Business

Do you have strong credit control experience within the recruitment sector - ideally supporting a temp/contract-led business operating across multiple international markets?

If so, this is a particularly interesting opportunity to take on a broader and more strategic remit than a traditional Credit Control Manager role.

Our client is a growing international recruitment business looking to appoint an experienced Credit Control/Credit Risk & Working Capital Manager to review and strengthen the way it manages client exposure, commercial risk, funding relationships and credit-control processes across its international operations.

Importantly, this is NOT a business with a significant aged-debt problem.

The focus is much more forward-looking: understanding where risk sits, whether existing processes and structures are fit for future growth, and ensuring the business is making well-informed commercial decisions around the clients it chooses to work with and the terms it accepts.

The role will include:

Reviewing the existing credit-control function, processes, systems and team structure.

Taking a pragmatic, hands-on approach when required - getting into the detail of individual accounts, invoices, processes and issues rather than operating purely at a strategic level.

Assessing client exposure across different international markets and identifying where concentrations of risk may exist.

Working with senior stakeholders to understand whether individual contracts and client relationships represent genuinely good business from a cash, risk and working-capital perspective.

Challenging extended payment terms where appropriate, particularly where larger clients seek to impose terms that may be commercially unattractive.

Looking beyond headline revenue to consider the wider implications of client terms, payment behaviour and funding requirements.

Reviewing relationships with invoice-discounting providers across different territories and ensuring facilities remain appropriate for the business.

Understanding the interaction between client contracts, billing processes, funding arrangements and cash collection.

Identifying operational weaknesses that could create future collection or cash-flow issues even where no current debt problem exists.

Reviewing recurring administrative or contractual issues that can delay payment, create unnecessary rework or expose the business to avoidable risk.

Helping the business establish clearer controls around billing entities, contractual information, invoicing requirements and client onboarding.

Reviewing the current Credit Control team and identifying opportunities to strengthen, reshape or develop the existing team.

Improving reporting and visibility around debtor exposure, client concentration, payment terms, DSO and working-capital risk.

Identifying opportunities for automation and process improvement.

Developing a more scalable framework that can support continued international expansion.

What we're looking for

Recruitment-sector experience is particularly important for this appointment.

You'll ideally have worked within a temp or contract-led recruitment business and understand the relationship between client contracts, timesheets, payroll, billing, invoice discounting, working capital and cash collection.

International experience would be highly advantageous, particularly where you've dealt with different funding providers, client structures, currencies and payment practices across several territories.

We're looking for someone who can operate above the day-to-day ledger, but who is equally comfortable getting into the weeds when required. This is a strategic role, but it is not a purely advisory one: you'll need to be pragmatic, hands-on and prepared to work through the detail yourself in order to understand issues, challenge effectively and drive practical improvements.

You'll be comfortable asking questions such as:

Are we taking on the right type of business?

Are the payment terms commercially sensible?

Is our exposure to a particular client becoming too high?

Are our funding arrangements appropriate in each market?

Are our contracts and billing processes protecting us from avoidable delays?

Is the current team structure right for where the business is heading?

What could become a problem six or twelve months from now if we don't address it today?

You'll combine strong technical credit-control knowledge with commercial judgement, curiosity and the confidence to challenge established ways of working.

Permanent or Fixed-Term?

The current intention is for this to be a permanent appointment.

That said, our client recognises that the nature of the role may also appeal to someone who specialises in transformation, review and improvement projects.

For the right individual, they would therefore be open to considering a 12-month fixed-term contract if that structure is better suited to the candidate and the assignment.

Given the high volume of responses we receive from the combination of job boards, social media and other sources and despite our best efforts, many of our responses will be via email as we simply can't call every application - We know that's not what you want to hear but we hope you'll understand?

Short-listed candidates will obviously be contacted for this specific role, and if you haven't heard from us within a week, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion.

We will keep your CV on file to contact you with regards to future roles and any other advice to help you, however if you do not wish to remain on our database, please let us know and we will obviously remove you. Alternatively, please feel free to contact us for a chat

title: Finance & HR Officer
description:
HR & Finance Officer
- Salary: £38,068 per annum
- Location: On-site in a primary school setting
- Job Type: Full-time, fixed-term contract until 31/08/2027, term time only
- Hours: 35 hours per week

We are seeking an organised and detail-focused HR Finance Officer to provide high-quality human resources and financial administration support within a busy primary school environment. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced HR Finance Officer to support school leadership through effective financial processes, compliant HR administration, and a strong commitment to safeguarding. The contract is fixed term until 31/08/2027, with the role to be reviewed and potentially made permanent.

Day-to-day of the role
- Support the preparation of the annual school budget, monitor expenditure, and highlight any variances.
- Process purchase orders, invoices, and expense claims in line with school financial procedures.
- Manage income collection for items such as dinner money, school trips, and wraparound care through online payment systems.
- Carry out monthly bank reconciliations and maintain accurate records on financial management systems.
- Assist with the preparation of financial returns for the local authority, trust, or governing body.
- Coordinate recruitment activity, including placing adverts, managing applications, arranging interviews, and preparing offer documentation.
- Maintain the Single Central Record and complete all required pre-employment checks, including DBS and references.
- Collate monthly payroll changes, monitor staff absence records, and respond to routine HR policy and contract queries.

Required skills & qualifications
- NVQ Level 3 or above in Business, Finance, HR, or equivalent practical experience.
- Professional qualifications such as AAT, CIPD or similar would be advantageous.
- Previous experience in an HR or finance administration role, ideally within education or the public sector.
- Good working knowledge of school systems such as SIMS, Arbor or FMS, along with MS Office applications.
- Strong numerical, administrative, and organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Ability to handle sensitive information with complete confidentiality and professionalism.
- Confident communication skills and the ability to work effectively with school leaders, staff, and external contacts.
- Clear commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.

Benefits
- Term-time only working pattern.
- Fixed-term opportunity until 31/08/2027 with potential to become permanent following review.
- Salary of £38,068 per annum.
- Opportunity to play a key role in supporting both finance and HR operations in a school setting.

How to apply

To apply for this HR Finance Officer position, please submit your CV outlining your relevant experience and suitability for the role. In your CV, please highlight your experience in HR administration, finance processes, and working within a school or public sector environment.

title: Office Manager/ Sales Administrator
description:
Pear recruitment: Office Manager/ Sales Administrator

Location: Marylebone

Salary: Up to £35,000

Hours: Monday - Friday 9am-6pm

Our client, one of London's premier estate agents, is seeking an experienced Office Manager & Sales Administrator to join their dynamic and friendly team. This is a full-time office-based role, Monday - Friday, 09:00-18:00, based in central London.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an organised and proactive professional with a strong administrative background to become a valuable asset to their sales team.

About the Role

Reporting to the Office Director and Sales Manager, you'll thrive in a fast-paced and exciting environment, handling sales-related administration and appointment scheduling while providing essential support to the team.

What they are Looking For

The ideal candidate will be efficient, adaptable, and highly organised, with excellent administrative abilities, strong customer service skills, and a working knowledge of spreadsheets. Prior experience in a similar role is highly desirable.

Key Responsibilities Sales Support:
- Providing secretarial and administrative support to the sales team
- Issuing memorandums of sale and invoices upon exchange of contracts
- Preparing marketing materials, including brochures and window cards
- Organising canvassing materials and booking market appraisals
- Conducting AML checks for all clients

Office Management
- Providing HR support, including onboarding new starters, preparing contracts, and maintaining HR documentation
- Welcoming clients and visitors, assisting with registration and inquiries
- Handling customer service requests, orders, and complaints
- Managing inbound office calls
- Supporting the Director with diary management, scheduling, and correspondence
- Managing paperwork, emails, and phone calls on behalf of the Director
- Acting as the first point of contact for the Director when required
- Organising company events (e.g., Christmas parties, work trips, and team-building activities

What You'll Need
- Prior experience as a Sales Administrator or Office Manager in a sales environment
- Excellent organisation and multitasking skills
- Strong attention to detail and ability to work to tight deadlines
- Confident communication skills with a friendly and professional approach
- HR experience is preferred but not essential
- A full UK driving license is desirable but not required

If you are interested in this Office Manager/ Sales Administrator position and would like to know more, please email your CV or telephone us on a strictly private and confidential basis.

Due to the number of responses we receive to our advertisements we are unfortunately unable to respond individually to each applicant. If you do not hear from us within 7 days you may assume you have not been selected this time - but please apply for anything you feel you are suitable for and thank you for your interest in PEAR Recruitment.

Confidentiality - All communication with us is treated with the upmost confidentiality and you will always be advised if your CV is being submitted to a client.
